title: eriogonum microtheca subsp. rigidum
intro: Eriogonum microtheca subsp. rigidum, commonly known as Mormon tea, is a subspecies of the Eriogonum microtheca plant, belonging to the Polygonaceae family. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include acting as a diuretic, lowering blood pressure, and alleviating symptoms of arthritis and other inflammatory conditions. The therapeutic actions of Eriogonum microtheca subsp. rigidum are attributed to its ability to act as an anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial agent, which can help to protect against cell damage and infection. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
